questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I am studying Forest and Nature Management, I wanted to learn about the Nature in Australia as it is very unique and their way of managing it. It was also important to me to learn about a different culture and how to interact with people with diverse backgrounds.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNSW is a great university and the whole experience for exchange students is very well organized. they create opportunities for exchange students to meet and get to know each other.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy as UNSW organized an international day event where they informed us about important topics and introduced us to the university and the different services.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an exchange student course, in which the professors were very helpful in preparing us for the following courses, in how to use the school platform and the Australian culture.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy because I already knew someone who lives in Sydney

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Transport in Sydney is not the best and therefore living off campus may translate into a long commute time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was straightforward but each system is quite different and therefore requires some time to get accustomed to. Also some courses were hard to register to.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In the platform, one can register to courses on a given date. It is important to know the date as classes get filled up very fast. One problem was that one of the courses that had been approved , was suddenly cancelled and so when I tried to select a different course, they were all almost full or already full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: One can call the "student service" to require help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was tricky as one of my courses was cancelled last minute which made it harder to select other courses as they were mostly full. Also the date of registration wasnt so clearly advertised.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To get many courses approved and to be aware of the date by which to register beforehand

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors were very kind and helpful

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were challenging and interesting.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was nice to have the opportunity to listen to many guest lecturers. Also the fact that courses are recorded, makes it easier for students whose mother tongue is not english to follow and learn.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Sydney environment

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Rethinking the environment
Project Management 
Conservation Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Sydney environment because it is a good way to learn about the place that you are visting and includes also interesting field trips such as learning about the aboriginal culture

questions.answer: there is a gym, a swimming pool and many sport clubs such as surfing

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: scuba diving and surfing

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to national parks and beaches

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was easy as it is very multicultural

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Australians seem very easy going and sociable

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The effect of how aboriginal people were treated in the past has an impact on the culture of today

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the diversity

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
get to know other exchange students so you can organize trips together,
learn about the clubs so as to join fun activities
be aware that semesters go by fast so it is important to keep track of time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The lecture recordings really helped me with understanding the english

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new students from round the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: understanding the thick australian accent of some people and understanding the new system
